intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital nonprogressive movement disorder with ataxia and eye movement abnormalities (CONMAE) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the ESRRG gene (602969) on chromosome 1q41.

paragraphs.text: Congenital nonprogressive movement disorder with ataxia and eye movement abnormalities (CONMAE) is a nonprogressive congenital movement disorder. Its main features are motor developmental delay, muscular hypotonia, eye movement disorders, and congenital ataxia or gait imbalance. Some patients also have joint hyperflexibility, dysarthria, myopia, and growth delay (Bresack et al., 2025).

paragraphs.text: Bresack et al. (2025) described 8 individuals from 7 unrelated families with a nonprogressive congenital movement disorder with ataxia. All of them had motor developmental delay, muscular hypotonia, eye movement disorders, and congenital ataxia or gait imbalance. Other features included joint hyperflexibility, dysarthria, myopia, and growth delay.

paragraphs.text: Bresack et al. (2025) identified heterozygous mutations in the ESRRG gene in 8 individuals from 7 unrelated families with a nonprogressive congenital movement disorder with ataxia. Most of the mutations occurred de novo. The reported mutations included 5 missense mutations: G137E, K149R, C180Y, R184C, and L449R. The sixth was a 1-bp duplication (c.1352dup) that caused a frameshift (L451Ffs*38). None of the variants was present in gnomAD v4.1. All were predicted to be deleterious in silico and were located in intolerant segments of the protein.

paragraphs.text: In functional studies, Bresack et al. (2025) found that all of the variant proteins localized correctly to the nucleus. However, each significantly reduced transcriptional activity in an ERRE reporter assay. Knockout of ESRRG significantly increased the proliferation rate of HEK293T cells. Wild-type ESRRG restored normal proliferation in the knockout cells, but none of the patient variants did. Molecular modeling also suggested that the variants reduce protein function.

paragraphs.text: Bresack et al. (2025) found that ESRRG knockout significantly increased the proliferation rate of HEK293T cells. Wild-type ESRRG restored normal proliferation, whereas none of the patient variants did. The variant proteins localized correctly to the nucleus but showed significantly reduced transcriptional activity in an ERRE reporter assay. Molecular modeling also suggested reduced protein function. Together, these results indicated that the variants cause a loss of ESRRG function.

paragraphs.text: Bresack et al. (2025) found a heterozygous c.410G-A transition in the ESRRG gene in a patient with a nonprogressive congenital movement disorder with ataxia. The mutation results in a gly137-to-glu (G137E) substitution. It was absent from gnomAD v4.1, was predicted to be deleterious in silico, and lay in an intolerant segment of the protein. In an ERRE reporter assay the variant showed reduced transcriptional activity. It also failed to restore proliferation in ESRRG-knockout HEK293T cells.
